title: Serving Efficiency Portfolio: Adaptive Serving Profiles (batching, caching, quantization)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create and track an initiative that coordinates cross-functional delivery of adaptive serving profiles — a set of runtime-configured bundles (batching thresholds, prefix/KV cache policies, and quantization profiles) that automatically optimize cost/perf per customer workload. The goal is to produce deployable profiles, an evaluation harness, and rollout plan so Product, Runtime, and Console teams can measure realized savings against OKRs.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 canonical serving profiles (latency-sensitive, balanced, cost-sensitive) with concrete parameter sets for batching, cache TTL/eviction, and quantization profiles
Implement measurement plan: p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens for each profile across at least 5 representative workloads
Create console UI mock (Console-UX) to expose profile selection and per-route savings estimates
Run a canary rollout on Dedicated with automatic fallback and verify no customer-facing errors for 48h
Document runbook for profile tuning and add evaluation checks to release gating
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: Kickoff notes — aligned on three profile tiers and measurement metrics. Action: ENG to prototype batching knobs; Console PM to do quick mock.
2025-02-21 Ravi Patel: ENG provided initial batching knobs and a KV cache policy matrix. Noted trade-off: aggressive batching increases p99 under bursty traffic — need fallback policy.

2025-02-27 Aria Gomez (Eng): Prototype quantization experiment results: q4_0 gives 18-22% cost reduction with minor quality regressions on long-context completion tests. Suggested gated rollout for q4_0 on cost-sensitive profile.
2025-03-03 Ben Kline (Console-UX): Uploaded Console mock to Drive: https://drive.company/serving/profiles/mock_v1 — shows per-route estimated savings and expected latency delta.
2025-03-05 Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to require canary stability for 48h and explicit fallback policy. Added ENG-7312 as dependency for autoscaling behavior during batching spikes.
notes: Measurement plan details: compare profiles against baseline across 5 corpora (chat, code-completion, search-summaries, embeddings heavy, long-form generation). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost/1M tokens, quality delta (ROUGE/BERTScore for long-form, pass-rate for safety checks).

Trade-offs recorded: aggressive KV caching reduces repeated prompt cost but increases memory pressure — require autoscaler headroom. Quantization gains vary by model family; add model-compatibility table before rollout.
Rollout plan: start with internal tenants -> opt-in customers -> limited Dedicated pools -> full rollout. Each stage gated by quality regressions and latency SLOs.
